evidenceCatalog.claim: TBCL Level 1 describes understanding and using simple words and phrases relating to daily life; its listening and speaking descriptors include simple personal-life information and time/quantity language. This supports a broad capability comparison, not the exact proposal sequence.
The official Level 1 vocabulary reference lists the candidate forms 今天 and 星期一. This is a one-item-at-a-time reference lookup only; no vocabulary table, definition, or example is reproduced.
The official Level 1 grammar lookup classifies a copula point at Level 1. It supports considering a copula candidate, not this target's productivity or placement.

CCCC is designed for mostly non-Chinese-speaking children aged 7–12 and lists time/space among broad child-life topics. This does not establish an item-level vocabulary list, lesson order, or rights to test content.
The official download page identifies CC BY-SA 4.0 and requires attribution and share-alike for modified data. The latest release page observed for this proposal is dated 2026-09-10.
CC-CEDICT-backed MDBG lookup for 今天, Pinyin jīntiān, glossed as today.
CC-CEDICT-backed MDBG lookup for 星期一, Pinyin Xīngqīyī, glossed as Monday.
CC-CEDICT-backed MDBG lookup for 是 with Pinyin shì and a to-be gloss. No entry examples are copied.

A learner may benefit from hearing and communicating one calendar statement, then mapping its words visually, then recognizing the script. This sequence is a testable TongXuan hypothesis, not a framework requirement.
Per-character recognition review is a candidate SRS grain for this experiment. Exact backend linkage, intervals, and mastery effects require separate checks and remain unimplemented.

The current graph distinguishes listening, pronunciation, speaking, character recognition, and writing; exposure does not imply a writing requirement. This proposal tests no executable task or mastery rule.

variants.label: Communication-first

lessons.title: Prototype A — Listening + pronunciation
lessons.whyNow: Start by hearing and saying only the two time labels. The calendar meaning and copular sentence are deferred so this proposal has an observable oral-first stage.
lessons.orderRationale: Communication-first introduces the two selected Level 1 lexical candidates in speech before visual matching or grammar production.
alternatives: Introduce only 今天 first and move 星期一 to Prototype B; this lowers first-slot lexical load but weakens a paired oral comparison.

confidence.rationale: This ordering is a hypothesis, not an official level sequence.

lessons.adaptiveLearningFit: A future authoritative queue could keep both lexical prerequisites in order and allow only policy-approved repetition; adaptive ranking must not reorder or select a next lesson autonomously.

riskFlags: Two new words and five syllables arrive in the first slot; no threshold is inferred.

lessons.title: Prototype B — Vocabulary + visual recognition
lessons.whyNow: The child has already heard both labels, so this slot asks whether the meanings can be mapped visually without also requiring Chinese script recognition.
lessons.orderRationale: Visual-semantic matching follows oral introduction and precedes productive sentence work.
alternatives: Show Chinese word forms in this slot; that would mix semantic visual matching with character recognition and is excluded from this variant.

confidence.rationale: Separating visual meaning from character recognition is a proposal design choice.

lessons.adaptiveLearningFit: Repeat a visual meaning task only against these two fixed targets; no new target is inferred from success or error.

lessons.title: Prototype C — Sentence pattern + speaking
lessons.whyNow: Only after the two lexical meanings are familiar does this proposal add a receptive and productive copular relation.
lessons.orderRationale: This is the key communication-first decision: speaking occurs before the separate character-recognition/SRS slot.
alternatives: Move the copula into Prototype A as listening-only and require speaking after character recognition, as in Variant B.

confidence.rationale: TBCL supports considering a Level 1 copula but does not select this frame or productive timing.

lessons.adaptiveLearningFit: The queue must verify both vocabulary prerequisites before this candidate speaking task; adaptive ranking cannot bypass that dependency.

riskFlags: The copula's spoken production requirement is a major unresolved teaching choice.

lessons.title: Prototype D — Character recognition + SRS
lessons.whyNow: After oral sentence work, this slot introduces the six visible characters as recognition-only candidates and explores one-character SRS items.
lessons.orderRationale: Recognition and SRS follow communication so script exposure does not delay the oral experiment.
alternatives: Use whole-word SRS items instead of six individual characters; this may reduce item count but changes the SRS contract.

confidence.rationale: Neither six-character load nor character-level SRS is validated by real learners.
limitations: Character-level SRS identity and intervals are not implemented here.

lessons.adaptiveLearningFit: If ever approved, REVIEW must address only exact character targets and remain separate from new curriculum selection; no interval or mastery effect is proposed.

riskFlags: Six new character forms in one slot may be high load; no threshold is available.

lessons.title: Prototype E — Integrated LEARN + REVIEW + REPAIR
lessons.whyNow: The final slot reuses only the proposal's prior targets to test the integrated mode contract; it adds no new curriculum target.
lessons.orderRationale: Integration is last so REVIEW and REPAIR can refer to an exact earlier target set.
alternatives: End after Prototype D; that would not test the required integrated LEARN/REVIEW/REPAIR capability.

confidence.rationale: The mode mix is a feasibility hypothesis, not a validated review policy.
limitations: No SRS interval, mastery settlement, or reward policy.

lessons.adaptiveLearningFit: A future queue may surface only approved due items for these exact targets; repair must reuse prior approved targets and cannot autonomously choose new content.

riskFlags: Mixed-mode task and review policy requires a separate executable contract audit.

strengths: Separates oral introduction, visual meaning, productive grammar, script recognition, and later review.
Makes the speaking-before-script sequencing decision visible.
risks: C delays script support until after productive speaking.
Six character targets are introduced together.
variants.cognitiveLoadSummary: New load by order A→E: vocabulary 2, 0, 0, 0, 0; grammar 0, 0, 1, 0, 0; character recognition 0, 0, 0, 6, 0; writing 0 in every slot; phonetic syllables 5, 0, 1, 0, 0. No universal load threshold is asserted.
variants.adaptiveLearningFit: A conservative authoritative queue can enforce the declared prerequisites and modes. Adaptive recommendation remains read-only and cannot choose or reorder the next target; this plan does not change that policy.

confidence.rationale: The target identities have traceable source evidence, but variant superiority and learner outcomes are unknown.

variants.label: Phonetic/recognition-balanced

lessons.title: Prototype A — Listening + pronunciation
lessons.whyNow: The copular form is heard and understood receptively with the two words in the first slot; speaking the full frame is deliberately deferred.
lessons.orderRationale: This variant balances phonetic and grammatical listening input early, then schedules character recognition before productive sentence use.
alternatives: Delay 是 until Prototype C as in Variant A; that lowers first-slot load but leaves no receptive grammar preparation.

confidence.rationale: This is an intentional sequencing comparison, not a level requirement.
limitations: Three target units and six syllables appear in the first slot.

lessons.adaptiveLearningFit: A queue could allow recognition support before the speaking prerequisite only if the Owner approves this order; adaptive ranking must not invent or reorder it.

riskFlags: Highest first-slot oral/phonetic load across the variants.

lessons.title: Prototype B — Vocabulary + visual recognition
lessons.whyNow: The two meanings are already known aurally, so the same visual-semantic mapping as Variant A can be compared before script recognition.
lessons.orderRationale: This preserves a separate non-script visual vocabulary slot and prevents visual meaning from being conflated with reading.
alternatives: Display the Chinese forms here; that would add character exposure before the explicitly tracked character-recognition/SRS slot.

confidence.rationale: Separating visual meaning from script recognition is a proposal design choice.

lessons.adaptiveLearningFit: Repeat only the two fixed meaning targets; no new vocabulary is selected from visual success or failure.

lessons.title: Prototype D — Character recognition + SRS
lessons.whyNow: The child has already heard the full sentence relation, then receives script recognition/SRS support before being asked to produce the full sentence.
lessons.orderRationale: This is the balanced variant's key choice: receptive grammar and character recognition both precede speaking.
alternatives: Move this slot after Prototype C, as in Variant A, so all character recognition follows productive communication.

confidence.rationale: The sequence is designed for comparison; the six-character load and SRS grain are unvalidated.

lessons.adaptiveLearningFit: If approved, queue only these exact recognition candidates before the speaking task; this is a fixed plan, not a recommendation engine change.

riskFlags: Six new character forms arrive in one slot.

lessons.title: Prototype C — Sentence pattern + speaking
lessons.whyNow: After the same receptive vocabulary, grammar, and character candidates, the learner now tries the one oral frame.
lessons.orderRationale: Speaking is deliberately delayed until both phonetic input and character-recognition/SRS exposure have occurred.
alternatives: Allow speaking after only receptive word and grammar input, as in Variant A.

confidence.rationale: No evidence here proves character recognition improves or should precede speaking.

lessons.adaptiveLearningFit: The authoritative sequence must enforce all listed prerequisites; adaptive recommendation may not skip recognition because of a model score.

riskFlags: Possible interference: recognizing six script forms before producing a sentence could increase load.

lessons.title: Prototype E — Integrated LEARN + REVIEW + REPAIR
lessons.whyNow: Integration comes last and only reuses the exact target identities from the earlier slots.
lessons.orderRationale: This preserves the same integrated-flow experiment while keeping order difference isolated to speaking and character support.
alternatives: Do not include a mixed LEARN/REVIEW/REPAIR slot; that fails to test the required integrated capability.

confidence.rationale: The task-mode sequence is not implemented or child-validated.
limitations: No SRS interval, mastery settlement, or reward policy.

lessons.adaptiveLearningFit: Only exact approved due items may be reviewed; repair reuses already approved candidates and never generates the next lesson.

riskFlags: Mixed-mode contract needs a separate technical review.

strengths: Presents receptive grammar early and character recognition before productive speaking.
Makes phonetic, semantic-visual, and script recognition loads separately countable.
risks: Prototype A has the highest first-slot lexical, grammar, and phonetic load.
Six character candidates are clustered before speaking.
No empirical evidence says this order is better.
